name: defiance
quote: I don't care, I'm going anyway.
description: Openly taking an action (or inaction) despite knowing that it's against the desires of a particular person or group.
perceptions: A person or group wants me to do or not do something.
I'm going to do it anyway.
I'm not going to hide that I'm doing it.
examples: The teenager texted her mom from the mall despite being told not to go.

guidance.description: Defiance, which can look like resistance or outright disobedience, is an exaggerated expression of independence or differentiation from the family. By pushing against something, adolescents and young adults are trying to figure out who they are and define themselves in their own identity.

variations.name: disobedience
variations.description: Action or inaction against the desires of a particular person or group, whether on purpose or not.
perceptions: A person or group wants me to do or not do something.
I forgot about it, or I'm going to do it anyway.
examples: The teenager snuck off to the mall despite being told not to go.

variations.name: insubordination
variations.description: Action or inaction against the desires of a particular person of higher rank than you.
perceptions: A person or group with more authority wants me to do or not do something.
I'm going to do it anyway.
examples: The employee took a long lunch despite being told by the manager to work through lunch.

guidance.description: 5 Examples of Insubordination in the Workplace (With Tips)

variations.name: unapologetic
variations.description: A perception that someone expects you to feel bad about something you did or should do, but you do not.
perceptions: Someone wants me to do something or apologize for something.
It was not really my fault or they had enough warning.
I do not regret the action.
examples: Giving plenty of warning time about changing the picnic date but someone complains.
Hurting someone accidentally but not expressing regret.

guidance.description: Being 'unapologetic' can mean being authentic. Here are some references with that vibe.
Being 'unapologetic' can also mean being rude. If this an issue in your world, here are some references.

variations.name: disagreement
variations.description: Rejecting an outcome proposed by someone else. This can lead you to take action against the proposal or you may be silent.
perceptions: I can choose to allow it to happen or reject it.
I may take action against it.
examples: Not wanting to go to the restaurant your sibling suggested.
Having a heated conversation about who gets to host the holiday party.

guidance.description: Conflict triggers strong emotions and can lead to hurt feelings, disappointment, and discomfort. When handled in an unhealthy manner, it can cause irreparable rifts, resentments, and break-ups. But when conflict is resolved in a healthy way, it increases your understanding of the other person, builds trust, and strengthens your relationships.
guidance.attribution: Jeanne Segal, Ph.D., Lawrence Robinson and Melinda Smith, M.A.

comparisons.description: The differences between these three are subtle and they're often used interchangeably. 'Disobedience' is the general term for not following a rule or request. It can be willful or accidental. 'Defiance' is a bold and open form of disobedience. 'Insubordination' is disobeying a rule or request from a higher ranked person in a hierarchy.

commentaries.quote: Insubordination may only be the evidence of a strong mind.
Insubordination goes beyond mere disagreement — it’s a willful defiance that can affect team morale, productivity, and trust in leadership.
Defiance is beautiful. The defiance of power, especially great or overwhelming power, exalts and glorifies the rebel.
I am no longer accepting the things I cannot change.
Do a search for quotes about disobedience. The sheer volume of people extolling the virtues of defiance says a lot. And it suggests that Pandora is here to stay.
The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.
We don't necessarily always agree, but hopefully we make each other think, and that's what matters.
